extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal education funds (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, legal counsel, and other stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble to the Department of Education's final Title IX regulations responding to public comments and explaining the Department's decisions on provisions such as transition plans, athletics adjustment periods, parental rights, religious exemptions, transparency, and rulemaking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition plan provisions (§§106.2(s), 106.16, 106.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department removed provisions requiring transition plans in §§106.2(s), 106.16, and 106.17 because they are outdated and describe requirements that are no longer operative or necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions originally governed the transition of certain single-sex institutions to coeducational institutions in the years immediately following the 1975 regulations. The Department states removal of these provisions does not affect Title IX's coverage of gender identity discrimination; §106.2(s) was removed because the defined term no longer appears in the regulations after removal of §§106.16 and 106.17.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment period for athletics (§106.41(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Current §106.41(d) required recipients to come into compliance with the original athletic regulations within three years of the 1975 effective date; the Department removed §106.41(d) because that adjustment period has passed and the provision is no longer operative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The removal does not change other provisions governing athletics. The effective date for other amended provisions is discussed elsewhere (Effective Date and Retroactivity, Section VII.F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and specificity of regulations as a policy objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department determined that greater clarity and specificity in the final regulations will better equip recipients to create and maintain school environments free from sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In response to commenters who found the proposed regulations vague or ambiguous, the Department reviewed comments and, where appropriate, revised regulatory text or addressed concerns in the preamble. The Department cites identification of prohibited bases (§106.10), duties of employees (§106.44), and detailed grievance procedures (§§106.45 and 106.46) as examples of clarity improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.10 — Bases of prohibited sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department 'has identified bases of prohibited sex discrimination' in the final regulations to clarify Title IX protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the detailed discussion of §106.10 in the preamble for the specific bases the Department recognizes as constituting sex discrimination; this identification is part of the Department's effort to give recipients clear understanding of rights and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.44 — Duties of recipients' employees (reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations specifically articulate duties of recipients' employees, generally limiting teachers' duties to reporting information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination to the recipient's Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department notes §106.44 requires reporting to the Title IX Coordinator and that the obligations placed on employees are necessary to effectuate Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate; employees are required to receive annual training under §106.8(d) to adhere to these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: §§106.45 and 106.46 — Detailed grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations provide detailed grievance procedures for recipients to follow in addressing complaints of sex discrimination and sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These grievance procedures are intended to standardize and strengthen complaint processing and are discussed in detail elsewhere in the preamble and regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.8(d) — Annual Title IX training requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.8(d) requires annual Title IX training for employees so they can adhere to the regulations' requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department cites this requirement in response to concerns about teachers' roles and potential over-enforcement, emphasizing training is intended to ensure employees understand reporting duties and limits of their responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.6(g) — Preservation of parental legal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.6(g) affirms that nothing in the final regulations may be read in derogation of any legal right of a parent, guardian, or other authorized legal representative to act on behalf of a complainant, respondent, or other person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department relies on §106.6(g) to rebut concerns that the regulations diminish parental rights; the preamble explains that the regulations do not confer parental rights to others nor interfere with parents' liberty interests recognized by relevant Supreme Court precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.44(j)(2) — Permitted disclosures to parents
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(j)(2) permits disclosures of information obtained in the course of complying with Title IX to a minor student's parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department cites this provision to address concerns about parental access to information and states nothing in the regulations derogates a parent's FERPA right to review and inspect education records or interferes with teacher-parent communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.40(b)(3) — Duty to take actions upon notification of pregnancy
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.40(b)(3) recognizes a recipient's duty to take actions to prevent discrimination and ensure equal access upon notification by a parent of a minor student's pregnancy or related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by the Department to demonstrate how the regulations protect parental interests in matters involving minor students' pregnancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.42 — Regulations do not regulate curricula
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX regulations include an explicit limitation that nothing in the regulation shall be interpreted as requiring or prohibiting or abridging the use of particular textbooks or curricular materials (34 CFR 106.42).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department reiterates that it does not regulate curricula and that the final regulations do not interfere with parents' rights to decide curricula for their children; this is used to address commenters' concerns about imposition of values or curricula.

rubrics_metrics.name: FERPA and teacher-parent communication preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the final regulations derogates a parent's FERPA right to review and inspect education records or interferes with teacher-parent communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department emphasizes that the regulations are limited to Title IX and do not modify FERPA rights or ordinary teacher-parent interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-campus conduct and hostile environment (Tinker/Mahanoy context)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department disagrees that the final regulations interfere with parental control over off-campus conduct; courts (Mahanoy and Tinker) may allow school regulation of off-campus or online speech in certain circumstances where it creates a sex-based hostile environment on campus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble notes Mahanoy did not resolve the issue of disciplining off-campus online conduct that creates a hostile environment; Tinker’s standard may apply in certain circumstances, but the Department asserts nothing in the final regulations derogates parental control over off-campus conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.12 — Religious exemption (statutory basis and non-amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to amend §106.12, which implements Title IX's statutory religious exemption: Title IX 'shall not apply to an educational institution which is controlled by a religious organization if the application of [Title IX] would not be consistent with the religious tenets of such organization' (20 U.S.C. 1681(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department acknowledges opponents of the exemption but notes Congress enacted the exemption and the Department's 2020 amendments codified longstanding agency practice; the Department cannot broadly opine on application of the exemption to particular facts without fact-specific analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.12(c) — Criteria for showing control by a religious organization; burden
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.12(c) offers several ways for a recipient to show it is controlled by a religious organization, but recipients are not entitled to formal deference and bear the burden to establish eligibility and scope of any exemption; tenuous relationships to religious organizations are insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an institution is controlled by a religious organization, the relevant tenets are those of the religious organization (not personal beliefs of an official). Even where an exemption is asserted, OCR may investigate and make findings if the tenets do not address the conduct; a recipient cannot invoke a religious exemption to retaliate.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.12(b) — Process for assurance of religious exemption (pre-assertion and during investigation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.12(b), a recipient may, but is not required to, submit a written statement to OCR seeking assurance of a religious exemption prior to invoking it; a recipient may also assert an exemption during a pending OCR investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department believes this approach balances institutional burdens and statutory requirements. A recipient's statement seeking assurance must 'identify[ ] the provisions of [the regulations] that conflict with a specific tenet of the religious organization.' An assurance does not necessarily bar OCR from investigating complaints alleging improper application of an exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of religious exemption assurances (FOIA and posting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters and correspondence regarding OCR assurances of religious exemptions are subject to FOIA requirements and the Department posts correspondence regarding assurances of religious exemptions on its website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department cites FOIA rules (5 U.S.C. 552(a)(2)(D)) and its practice of making frequently requested records publicly available electronically as responsive to commenters' calls for transparency; prospective students may also inquire directly with recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious exemption scope — does not extend to individuals or non-controlled entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory religious exemption applies to educational institutions controlled by religious organizations and does not extend to student organizations, individual employees or students, or educational institutions not controlled by religious organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department reiterates that nothing in the final regulations requires or authorizes a recipient to infringe individuals' First Amendment or other constitutional rights and discusses intersection of sex-based harassment prohibition with First Amendment considerations elsewhere (§106.2 discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR assurance and complaint processing
rubrics_metrics.description: An OCR assurance of a religious exemption does not always preclude OCR from investigating complaints; OCR may investigate if allegations fall outside the scope of the exemption or if the controlling organization’s interpretation differs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If OCR determines a complaint's allegations fall within an assurance, OCR may contact the controlling organization to verify tenets; OCR will not recognize an exemption if the organization denies control or its interpretation differs materially from the institution's.

rubrics_metrics.name: 34 CFR 75.500(d) and 76.500(d) (grant-related religious organization protections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commenters urged rescission of 34 CFR 75.500(d) and 76.500(d), which prohibit public postsecondary institutions receiving Department grants from enforcing certain nondiscrimination policies against religious student organizations; the Department did not address these in the July 2022 NPRM and proposes rescinding them in a separate rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because these regulations are outside the scope of this Title IX rulemaking, the Department references a separate proposed rulemaking (88 FR 10857 (Feb. 22, 2023)) for those changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking process and public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department explains it was not required to conduct negotiated rulemaking for Title IX, but nevertheless solicited live and written comments via a June 2021 public hearing, listening sessions, and the July 2022 NPRM; hundreds of thousands of comments were received and posted on Regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department coordinated with OMB per Executive Order 12866 prior to publication. The preamble defends the Department's process against critiques that it deprived the public of adequate notice or opportunity to consider interrelated issues.
